text:
anika: Thinking out loud — proposal to add a lightweight "partition broker" between edge ingress and the enrichment/fanout layer. Purpose: do sticky routing + partition rebalancing centrally to reduce cross-tenant hotspots and avoid huge per-worker connection counts. Thoughts?
kevin: +1 for reducing connection churn. curious about ordering guarantees and how this interacts with our prefix/KV cache work.
maria: can you sketch the happy-path flow? is broker stateful per-tenant or per-shard?
anika: happy-path: edge -> broker (routes to a partition id) -> partition queue -> enrichers/consumers. Broker keeps lease map {partition -> pod} and can move partitions proactively. stateful per-shard (subset of tenant traffic) not per-tenant. aim is to reduce downstream routing table size.
sre-bot: deploy note: any stateful broker needs leader election and persistent leases. consider using existing coord service (ZK/etcd) or Redis streams.
kevin: what are the tradeoffs vs our current shared-queue approach? my list: sticky routing reduces cache misses (good), introduces single-point-of-latency for routing (bad), makes rebalancing harder. also how do we handle backpressure?
anika: agreed. thinking partition broker is horizontally sharded and only holds lightweight leases + routing hints. it doesn't buffer payloads (we keep payloads in edge blob store / small in-mem queue at partition consumer). broker only returns partition id and route target.
sam: so broker returns something like {partition_id, target_addr, version} and edge does direct TCP to target?
anika: yes. sample response: ```json
{"partition":"p-42","target":"10.2.3.45:9001","lease_expires":1680000000,"sig":"..."}
```
kevin: with direct connections we avoid double-hop, good. but atomically switching targets for partition requires join drain protocol. migration plan?
maria: also need to propagate billing context and sampling decisions. if partition moves mid-stream, we must ensure billing keys go with payload or are deterministically derived.
frank: short-term: include billing_key in the edge request header and sign it so consumers can trust it. long-term: deterministic partition assignment from billing_key so movement is rare.
anika: deterministic partitioning is the plan: hash(billing_key || namespace) -> partition_id. broker just exposes current owner for a partition.
kevin: Ok that reduces late-binding lookups. still worried about rebalancing cost when a node dies and partitions are reassigned — how to avoid flash cold caches?
sam: we can do staggered warmup: when broker assigns a new owner, it marks partition as warming for X seconds and routes a small percentage of traffic for caching priming, rest goes to fallback replicas.
maria: fallback replicas implies we maintain N replicas per partition. that's overhead but reduces user-visible blips. what's N? 2 for redundancy?
anika: N=2 initially (owner + follower). owner handles strong reads/writes, follower accepts some priming traffic during drain. followers maintain minimal KV prefetch.
kevin: follower prefetch sounds heavy. alternative: keep lightweight prefix cache shared via async replicator (eventually consistent) instead of full follower. cheaper but can have higher miss rate on failover.
frank: cost-wise, followers increase GPU memory for KV caches. prefer async replicator + priming traffic approach for cost-sensitive tenants, but let high-SLA tenants opt into 2-replica mode.
anika: agreed — expose mode per-customer: "single", "replicated", "replicated-high-sla". default single, opt-in for replicated.
sre-bot: note: different modes affect autoscaling, billing, and SLA docs. need mkdocs update if we ship.
maria: what about ordering? do we guarantee per-partition ordering? some telemetry relies on monotonicity.\anke?
sam: we should guarantee per-partition at-most-once ordering semantics best-effort. network retries may cause duplicates; consumers must be idempotent. we can attach monotonic seq numbers per-tenant to help dedupe.
kevin: seq numbers require stable producer identity and good clock ordering. edge can stamp monotonic counters per billing_key. potential hotspot if a single billing_key is high-QPS.
anika: we already have per-connection counters in the edge. for high-QPS single billing_key, recommend sharding within a tenant by adding subkeys or using request_hash. document guidance.
maria: sampling: where to decide? edge currently samples before enrichment. if broker routes based on partition id, sampling should remain at edge. broker doesn't change sampling semantics.
anika: yes sampling stays at edge. broker must propagate sample flags so downstream can skip heavy enrichment.
frank: failure modes: broker outage -> edge fallback to global hash -> degraded but still functional. important to surface metrics: broker_routing_latency, broker_cache_hit, partition_move_rate.
sam: and broker should emit partition ownership events to our observability pipeline for audit and postmortem timelines.
maria: migration plan? canary rollout: enable broker for a small % of edge nodes, observe cache hit rate and tail latency for enrichers. gradually increase, enable replicated mode for selected tenants.
anika: proposed rollout steps: 1) read-only broker that returns partition id only (edge still uses existing routing). 2) soft-route: edge uses broker suggestion but falls back. 3) hard-route with leader leases and direct connections. 4) enable replication modes per-tenant.
kevin: perf tests we need: partition lookup p99 < 2ms, reassign time < 10s, failover recovery < 30s, and no increase in enrichers p50/p95 > 10% for default tenants.
frank: also add cost model: estimated memory for followers per partition, ops for lease churn, and billing delta for replicated tenants.
anika: action items: @kevin prototype broker lease API (owner TTL, take/release, list partitions) — due EOW. @maria write migration playbook + docs. @frank run cost model for N=1/2/3. @sam add observability metrics spec. I'll draft an RFC update with these and the rollout plan.
maria: ack. I'll include rollback steps and example k8s annotations for canary.
kevin: ack. I'll spin a bench harness that simulates billing_key skew and partition hot-shifts.
sre-bot: reminder: coordinate infra tickets for etcd capacity if using leases.
anika: one more note: keep the broker API minimal and idempotent. edge should be resilient to transient errors. conversations about security: broker responses should be signed and short-lived to avoid spoofing.
frank: encryption + signing with edge bootstrap keys is fine. we'll add token rotation plan.
anika: short summary for the thread: introduce broker for sticky routing + partition leases, deterministic partitioning on billing_key, modes for replication per-tenant, staged rollout (read-only -> soft -> hard), metrics and cost modeling required, owners assigned.
maria: thanks — I'll sync with product on tenant opt-in UX next week. :thumbsup:
